summary: Monterey County ground-cabin lookout built 1935-36 by the CCC on Ventana Double Cone; burned 1976-77; no fetched source describes the site today.

facts.design: 14x14 ground cabin on a rock foundation, California Region 5 Plan BC-301
facts.status_note: Burned in 1976 or 1977; no fetched source describes what remains

staffing.status: staffed around the clock by a pair of operators after the 1943 AWS cabin; last staffed in the 1960s

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS says the lookout burned under mysterious circumstances; Forest Lookouts, citing Reaves (1988), says vandals burned it. Both give 1976-77. Cause is recorded as disputed.
Forest Lookouts, citing Reaves, says materials were packed in by mules in 1942; FFLOS dates the cabin itself to 1943. Both years are kept.

notes_for_editor: Two fetched sources only. The story says nothing about the site today because no fetched page covers it. Unverified leads from search snippets (not fetched, so not cited): a 2005 climber report and a 2011 trip report describe stone foundation remains on the summit; a 1998 Ventana Wilderness Alliance article (ventanawild.org/news/ws98/dclook.html) reportedly dates the end to a mid-1960s lightning fire, which conflicts with the 1976-77 burning dates. That URL returned no text from the cache. A search snippet also reports the Forest Service main trail (2E04) closed for the 2026 Timber and Plaskett fires; not verified. firelookout.org's CA index lists Ventana Double Cone under FFLOS US 2040, CA 146, which differs from this record's US 1873, CA 68; possibly a duplicate record. The brief's 2019 registration date was not re-checked.
